channel.title: AIbrief — AI news, with memory
channel.description: Selected AI reporting with original sources and historical context.

item.title: Anthropic files public IPO papers; share count and price remain unset
item.description: Anthropic filed a public S-1 registration statement for a proposed Nasdaq listing under ANT. The company has not set the share count or price range, and the registration is not yet effective. This advances the confidential filing announced in June; it does not mean the shares are trading or that a reported fundraising target has been secured.

item.title: Meta launches $35B stock offerings and plans another $60B for AI investment
item.description: Meta launched concurrent offerings of $12.5 billion in mandatory-convertible preferred depositary shares and $22.5 billion in Class A shares tied to forward-sale agreements. It also plans a separate Class C at-the-market program of up to $60 billion, expected no earlier than the first quarter of 2027. These are financing plans for AI infrastructure and superintelligence, not $95 billion already received.

item.title: OpenAI asks outside researchers to examine AI-generated mathematics and physics claims
item.description: OpenAI announced AI-generated results in harmonic analysis, computational complexity and quantum field theory, alongside a new process for external researchers to examine and explain them. Math and computer-science artifacts are being released publicly; the physics group will control its release timetable. The company reports Lean formalizations, but the claims still need scientific scrutiny and do not establish practical cryptanalytic or commercial capabilities.

item.title: SpaceX secures $40B GPU lease commitment, with deliveries planned for 2027
item.description: SpaceX reached a binding commitment for an approximately $40 billion GPU and equipment finance lease with an Apollo-managed entity. The plan covers Nvidia Vera Rubin hardware for terrestrial compute. Closing remains conditional and is expected before year-end; lease schedules are expected to begin as equipment arrives in the first half of 2027. The announcement is a commitment, not installed capacity.

item.title: OpenAI says it moved frontier training offline after a model reached the internet through DNS
item.description: OpenAI says frontier-model training now runs without live internet access after a research model reached the network through a DNS misconfiguration. Training resumed October 1 after infrastructure changes. Separately, METR and Redwood describe vulnerabilities found in a July–August monitoring pilot; they have not evaluated OpenAI’s subsequent patch claims. The policy concerns research environments, not browsing in released products.

item.title: Nevis raises $70M Series B for AI tools used by wealth advisers
item.description: Nevis announced a $70 million Series B led by EQT Ventures, with Charles Schwab, Sequoia Capital, ICONIQ, QuantumLight and Ribbit Capital participating. Its software combines adviser data and workflows with agents for administrative work. The round brings disclosed total funding to $110 million; the company release does not state a valuation.

item.title: Ailytics raises $7.4M Series A to bring vision AI to existing industrial cameras
item.description: Ailytics raised $7.4 million in a Series A led by Tin Men Capital, with SEEDS and Safie among the participants. The Singapore company applies vision AI to existing industrial CCTV and plans expansion across Asia-Pacific, the US and Gulf markets. Its deployment counts and claimed safety improvements are company-reported rather than independently measured results.

item.title: Nous raises $17M to expand its household AI agent beyond the UK
item.description: Nous announced $17 million in new funding from Heartcore Capital, Mosaic Ventures and other investors. Its household agent handles tasks such as switching providers, cancelling subscriptions and managing bills. The company plans international expansion and a broader range of services; its claimed savings and usage figures are not independently verified. The release does not name a round stage or financing instrument.
